- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish (0.2–0.4), model frequently underestimates downward moves; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for downside risk.
- Model tends to lag in correcting for mean reversion; if 3–5 consecutive days show price below 30-day moving average, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% if sentiment >0.5 and price >10% below prior high.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model often overcorrects upward; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 periods.
